newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue-chip firms boost Morocco's stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip firms boost Morocco's stock exchange.

text.p: Morocco's main blue-chip companies, including ONA Group, boosted on Monday the Casablanca stock exchange, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 438.88 points, up 0.26 percent over the previous session.

"The main event on the market was the surge of ONA and Wafabank...As we noticed last week, the two stocks pursued their upward trend pushing at the same time the bourse index higher," Sanae Bennouna, a stockbroker at Upline Securities said.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate rose nine dirhams to 510 dirhams compared with the previous session.
ONA, showed a 20.6 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to 328.6 million dirhams in the period of January-June 1996 compared with 272.4 million dirhams in the first half of 1995.
ONA and its subsidiaries, including Cosumar sugar refinery, control between 65 and 80 percent of Morocco's sugar, edible oil, and milk market, stockbrokers said.
Cosumar gained 10 dirhams on Monday to close at 685 dirhams compared with last week.
Wafabank, one of the country's largest bank, rose seven dirhams to 527 dirhams.

The bank has a market capitalisation of 2.7 billion dirhams and registered a liquidity rate of 8.2 percent in the first half of the year, one of the highest rates on the market, an analyst at Wafa Bourse said.
Traded volume on the official market was 11.6 million dirhams, down from 23.8 million on the previous session, a bourse official said. ($1= 8.7 dirhams)
